explain.say: Leave a plant on a windowsill for a few days and it leans towards the glass. Plants cannot walk to the light, so they grow towards it instead. This is called phototropism.

faq.a: Auxin is a plant hormone, a chemical messenger made in the tips of shoots. It controls how much cells stretch, so moving it around lets a plant steer its growth.

faq.q: Why do plants grow towards light?
faq.a: Light is a plant's energy source for photosynthesis. Bending towards it puts the leaves in the brightest spot, so the plant can out-grow its shaded neighbours.
asks: Why do plants need to face the sun?

faq.a: Charles Darwin and his son Francis showed in 1880 that grass seedlings stopped bending when their tips were covered. They realised the tip senses light and sends a signal down, which later turned out to be auxin.
asks: What did Darwin find about plants and light?

faq.q: Why do plants grown in the dark get tall and pale?
faq.a: In the dark, a seedling puts its energy into growing tall quickly to reach light, and makes little chlorophyll. That is why it ends up spindly and yellow.
asks: What happens to a plant in a cupboard?

faq.q: Do roots grow towards light too?
faq.a: No. Most roots grow away from light and down towards gravity and water, which keeps them in the soil where they belong.

facts: Charles and Francis Darwin described their experiments on seedlings bending to light in The Power of Movement in Plants, 1880.
Auxin was the first plant hormone to be discovered.
Seedlings grown in darkness become tall, thin and pale, a condition called etiolation.

quiz.why: Auxin gathers on the shady side and makes its cells stretch more, so the stem curves towards the light.
